expectations.text: Declines to promise a winning ad: roughly 5% of creatives become winners at scale, a hit rate no brief can repeal

expectations.text: Frames the brief's job as maximising the quality, cleanliness and diversity of every at-bat rather than promising outcomes
expectations.evidence: "don't let 'did sprint 1-2 produce a winner' be the pass/fail gate on the process. Use it as a bonus outcome, not the test."

expectations.text: Gives the rebrief-rate target as under 20%, labelled a practical self-set target to tighten from the team's own history, not a researched constant

expectations.text: Puts brief-to-launch cycle time second, measured as two dates per brief, with the published benchmark of 10 business days or less

expectations.text: Judges the winner ratio against the team's own history rather than an absolute bar, given the roughly 5% base rate

expectations.text: Notes the re-rank condition: if a rolling results log already exists in the reporting stack, the ratio becomes free and moves to the top

expectations.text: Provides the diagnostic reads: a rising rebrief rate is a brief problem; a collapsing winner ratio with clean briefs is a concept-diversity problem
